            <abstract>Free-space electro-optic modulators are key to emerging photonic systems, yet their performance remains limited by trade-offs between modulation efficiency, bandwidth, and device aperture. Here we report a hybrid BaTiO3 (BTO)/TiO2 metasurface for large-aperture, efficient, gigahertz-speed free-space electro-optic modulation. Combining scalable BTO film growth by radio-frequency magnetron sputtering with mature TiO2 nanofabrication, we pattern the metasurface in TiO2 on an unetched BTO layer. The resulting devices support guided-mode resonances with quality factors exceeding 1300 and an optical confinement factor of ~0.8, while the continuous BTO layer makes efficient use of the applied voltage, together maximizing the overlap between the optical and driving fields within the BTO. A device with a 0.3 mm x 0.3 mm metasurface achieves a transmittance modulation efficiency of ~0.020 per volt and a -3 dB electro-optic bandwidth of ~0.8 GHz, with an effective Pockels coefficient of ~151 pm/V for the BTO. This establishes a scalable route to high-performance free-space electro-optic modulators for LiDAR, free-space optical communication, and reconfigurable optical computing.</abstract>
